title: Magic Hat

before.title: Magic Hat
before.text:
Tomás found an old hat in his grandmother's closet. The hat was blue and had a small star on it.

He put the hat on his head. Suddenly, a little bird flew out of the hat!

"Wow!" Said Tomás. He put the hat on again. This time, a small flower appeared in his hand.

Tomás was excited. He wanted to show his friends. He ran outside with the magic hat.

His friend Ana was playing near the tree. Tomás put on the hat again. A soft red ball rolled out onto the grass.

"This hat is magic!" Said Ana. They both laughed and played with the new things all afternoon.

That evening, Tomás put the hat back in the closet. He smiled, thinking about tomorrow's surprises.

The next day, he put the hat on again. But nothing happened. The magic hat was quiet now.

Tomás was not sad. He said, "Thank you, hat, for one wonderful day."

He kept the hat safe, hoping the magic would return again someday.

title: A Friend in the Tree

before.title: A Friend in the Tree
before.text:
Every morning, Lily walked past a big tree on her way to school. One day, she heard a small voice.

"Hello down there!" said the voice. Lily looked up. A small owl was sitting on a branch.

"Can you talk?" Asked Lily, very surprised.

"Yes," said the owl. "My name is Oliver. I live in this tree."

Lily was happy to meet a talking owl. Every day after that she stopped to talk with Oliver before school.

Oliver told her stories about the forest. Lily told him about her classroom and her friends.

One rainy day, Lily forgot her umbrella. Oliver flew down and covered her with his big wings until she reached the school door.

"Thank you, Oliver!" she said, laughing in the rain.

They became very close friends. Every morning and every afternoon, Lily and Oliver shared their small adventures together.

Years later, Lily still remembered her first friend in the tree.

title: The Little King

before.title: The Little King
before.text:
In a small village, there lived a boy named Marco. One day, he found a tiny golden crown in the garden.

He put the crown on his head just for fun. Suddenly, all the animals in the garden began to listen to him.

"Sit down, please," Marco said to a rabbit. The rabbit sat down right away.

Marco laughed. He was now the king of the garden! He told the birds to sing, and they sang a happy song.

Marco enjoyed being a little king, but he noticed the animals looked tired. He asked them, "Are you happy?"

The animals said they wanted to rest, not to follow orders all day.

Marco understood. He took off the crown and said, "You are free. I only wanted to play."

The animals were happy again. Marco learned that being kind was better than giving orders.

He kept the crown as a special memory, but he never wore it again.

title: Ants Work Together

before.title: Ants Work Together
before.text:
A group of ants lived under an old tree. Each one had a job. Some looked for food, and others carried it home.

A young ant named Sam was still learning. One day, he found a piece of bread that was much too heavy for him. He tried to move it alone, but it did not move.

Sam called for help. Three others came, and the four lifted the bread as a team. They took it home with ease.

Sam learned that asking for help was not a sign of being weak. A hard job could become easy when everyone worked as one.

title: A Bee and a Flower

before.title: A Bee and a Flower
before.text:
A small bee named Buzz flew over a garden. He was looking for sweet juice from flowers. He landed on a tall yellow flower and drank from it.

Yellow dust called pollen stuck to his legs. Buzz did not see it. He was busy getting food for the other bees at home.

Next, he flew to another flower. Some of the dust fell from his legs. He did this again and again. By moving the dust, Buzz helped the flowers make new seeds.

At the end of the day, he went back to his hive. He had food for the other bees. He had also helped the whole garden grow.

after.title: A Bee and a Flower
after.text:
A small bee named Buzz flew over a garden. She looked for nectar, a sweet drink from flowers. She landed on a yellow flower and drank.

Pollen, a fine powder, stuck to her body. Buzz did not notice it. She was busy collecting food for the bees at home.

Next, she flew to another flower. Some pollen from the first flower touched it. This can help a flower make seeds.

At the end of the day, Buzz went back to her hive with food. She had visited many flowers too.

reason: This is a named-bee episode, so classify it as animal fiction. Foraging honey bee workers are female; use she, identify nectar and explain that pollen on the body can reach another flower instead of asserting a guaranteed seed outcome.

title: Making Dinner

before.title: Making Dinner
before.text:
Every evening, Sara helped her father prepare dinner in their small kitchen. Tonight, they were making vegetable soup, one of her favorite meals.

"Can I cut the carrots?" Sara asked eagerly.

"Of course," her father replied, handing her a small, safe knife. "Just be careful and go slowly."

Sara carefully cut the carrots into small pieces while her father chopped onions and potatoes nearby. The kitchen soon filled with wonderful smells as everything cooked together in a large pot.

"What else do we need?" Sara asked, stirring the soup gently.

"Just a little salt and some fresh herbs," her father answered, adding them closely to the pot.

After about an hour, the soup was at last ready. Sara set the table while her father poured the warm soup into bowls.

They sat down together, and Sara proudly tasted her creation. "This is delicious!" she said happily.

Her father smiled. "You did a great job helping tonight. Cooking together is always more fun."

Sara agreed fully, already looking forward to helping prepare dinner again tomorrow evening.

Sara stirred the soup while her father watched. He added a little salt and some herbs. When the vegetables were soft, he poured the soup into bowls. Sara set the table.

"This is good," she said as they ate. She was glad they had made dinner together.

title: Why We Sleep

before.title: Why We Sleep
before.text:
Sleep gives our bodies time to rest. It also supports learning and memory.

After too little sleep, we may feel tired. Paying attention can be harder. Different people need different amounts of sleep. Age matters too.

A quiet bedtime routine can help us prepare for sleep. For example, we can put work away and read a little.

Sleep is part of everyday life, not time we have to earn by working hard.

title: How Rain Falls

before.title: How Rain Falls
before.text:
Rain begins with water on the ground. The sun warms water in seas, lakes, and rivers. Some of it changes into a gas and rises into the air.

The air is colder high above the ground. There, the gas turns back into tiny drops. Many drops gather and form a cloud.

Inside the cloud, the drops join and grow. At last, they become too heavy to stay in the sky. They fall as rain.

The water runs into the land, rivers, and seas. Later, the sun warms it again. Water keeps moving between the ground and the sky. This is called the water cycle.

title: Why Leaves Fall

before.title: Why Leaves Fall
before.text:
In spring and summer, leaves use light from the sun to make food for a tree. A green material in each leaf helps with this work.

In fall, the days grow shorter and the air gets cold. There is less light, so the tree stops making as much food. It no longer needs all its leaves.

As the green color goes away, yellow, orange, and red can be seen. The tree then closes the path that brings water to each leaf. The leaves dry and fall.

This helps the tree save energy in winter. When warm spring days return, new green leaves begin to grow.

after.title: Why Leaves Fall
after.text:
Many trees grow green leaves in spring. The leaves use sunlight to help make food for the tree. A green material called chlorophyll helps them do this.

In fall, days grow shorter. In some trees, the green color breaks down. Yellow and orange colors that were already in the leaves become easier to see. Some leaves also make a red color.

The tree begins to close the place where each leaf joins a branch. A leaf can then fall. In winter, the tree has no leaves to keep warm or supply with water. New leaves may grow in spring.

reason: Limit leaf fall to many deciduous trees, distinguish existing yellow/orange pigments from red pigment formed in some leaves, and use the relevant tree-and-season subtopic.

title: The Ant and the Grasshopper

before.title: The Ant and the Grasshopper
before.text:
All summer, an ant worked hard. She carried small pieces of food to her home.

A grasshopper watched her. He liked to sing and jump in the warm sun.

“Why do you work every day?” he asked. “There is food everywhere.”

The ant answered, “Winter will come. I want to be ready.”

The grasshopper laughed. He kept singing while the ant kept working.

Then winter came. The days became cold, and snow covered the ground. The grasshopper could not find food.

He went to the ant and asked for help.

The ant gave him some food. “You can stay warm here tonight,” she said. “But next summer, remember this winter.”

The grasshopper thanked her.

When warm days returned, he still sang. But this time, he also worked and saved food.
